subject: Extracting fitted values from Nmix model

messages.author: 797db90e8c0489d6
messages.subject: Extracting fitted values from Nmix model
parts:
Hello,

I am using R-INLA to fit an N-mixture model using family = "nmix"' as dicussed in https://arxiv.org/pdf/1705.01581.pdf.

I can see that using Out$summary.fitted.values will allow you to recover the estimates for the detection probabilities (p) in an N-mixture model, but is there an efficient way to recover the abundance estimate (N) means?

I could recover them using the model estimates for the "hyperparameters" (beta) but I wondered if there's another more direct way of getting these values.

Thank you,
SB

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Extracting fitted values from Nmix model
parts:
On Sun, 2017-08-13 at 08:15 -0700, SB wrote:
> Hello,
>
> I am using R-INLA to fit an N-mixture model using family = "nmix"' as
> dicussed in https://arxiv.org/pdf/1705.01581.pdf.
>
> I can see that using Out$summary.fitted.values will allow you to
> recover the estimates for the detection probabilities (p) in an N-
> mixture model, but is there an efficient way to recover the abundance
> estimate (N) means?
>
> I could recover them using the model estimates for the
> "hyperparameters" (beta) but I wondered if there's another more
> direct way of getting these values.

thanks for your email. the 'N' is summed out, so the only way is to use
the inla.posterior.sample() or better, inla.hyperpar.sample(), to
sample the 'beta's and then compute samples of lambda in the poisson
case, and then you know the conditional distribution for 'N' for each
sample.

H

--
Håvard Rue
he...@r-inla.org
